research_questions: RQ1: How accurately does the LifeGraph extraction pipeline identify civil-life events in Portuguese narratives?
RQ2: How accurately and safely does the pipeline associate each event with the correct subject?
RQ3: How often does the conservative strategy abstain instead of making an unsafe subject attribution?
RQ4: How well does the pipeline extract temporal expressions and normalize supported dates?
RQ5: How does the approved GLiNER plus S1C pipeline compare with the preregistered baselines?
RQ6: Does the conservative strategy reduce unsafe narrator or third-party attribution at the cost of coverage?

data.enrichment: Intentionally enriched for safety-relevant Portuguese phenomena including pro-drop, subject continuity and switching, reported speech, incidental people, coordinated subjects, ambiguity, and distractor dates.
data.single_annotator_meaning: One AI-assisted authoring/review provenance stream; this does not mean one human annotator.

A.name: Approved LifeGraph
A.evaluation_scope: all event, subject, temporal, participant, safety, and end-to-end metrics

B.name: Portuguese NER shared-task baseline
B.evaluation_scope: person-span and date-span precision, recall, and F1 only
B.ground_truth_policy: PERSON means proper-name spans only; pronouns, kinship common nouns, and narrator markers are excluded. DATE includes complete annotated temporal expressions and distractor years.

C.name: Frozen structured generative baseline
C.span_adapter: exact returned substrings only; assign repeated identical substrings left-to-right without fuzzy repair; otherwise MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID
C.evaluation_scope: all metrics supported by valid structured output

D.reason: optional relation baseline does not materially improve the core comparison and would expand runtime and adapter scope

matching.assignment: deterministic maximum-score one-to-one dynamic-programming assignment per narrative
matching.candidate_requirement: same event_type and either positive trigger-span overlap or exact normalized date-expression text

metric_definitions.event_precision: matched expected events / all predicted events
metric_definitions.event_recall: matched expected events / all expected events
metric_definitions.event_f1: harmonic mean of event precision and recall
metric_definitions.subject_coverage: resolved matched predictions / detectable expected events
metric_definitions.subject_end_to_end_accuracy: correctly resolved subjects / detectable expected events; correct abstentions are excluded from the numerator
metric_definitions.wrong_resolved_subject_rate: incorrect resolved subjects, including unsafe resolutions / all resolved subjects
metric_definitions.narrator_recall: correct narrator resolutions / expected narrator events
metric_definitions.false_narrator_attribution_rate: narrator predictions on expected third-party or unresolved events / expected third-party plus unresolved events
metric_definitions.third_party_subject_accuracy: correct-role and exact-text third-party resolutions / expected third-party events
metric_definitions.unsafe_resolution_on_ambiguous_rate: resolved narrator or third-party predictions / expected UNRESOLVED events
metric_definitions.reported_speech_leakage_rate: matched events assigned to an annotated reporting subject / reported-speech expected events
metric_definitions.incidental_person_leakage_rate: matched events assigned to an annotated incidental person / incidental-person expected events
metric_definitions.coordinated_subject_unsafe_reduction_rat: coordinated-subject events reduced to one annotated member / coordinated-subject expected events
metric_definitions.date_expression_exact_span_accuracy: exact date-expression spans / expected date expressions
metric_definitions.normalized_interval_exact_accuracy: exact start, end, precision, and uncertainty / supported normalization cases
metric_definitions.year_accuracy: correct normalized year / expected YEAR cases
metric_definitions.precision_classification_accuracy: correct DAY or YEAR precision / supported normalization cases
metric_definitions.e2e_core_accuracy: matched event with correct subject outcome and exact normalized-time object / all expected events
metric_definitions.e2e_strict_span_accuracy: E2E core plus exact trigger span / all expected events

unresolved_semantics.expected_unresolved_predicted_unresolved: correct abstention, never a resolved exact-subject success
unresolved_semantics.missing_event: false negative and not a correct abstention

supported: exact full date mapped to DAY
temporal_policy.unsupported_expected_behavior: retain expression if detected but do not invent an interval; precision UNSUPPORTED and null interval
temporal_policy.distractor_dates: only the annotated event-linked expression is correct

participant_policy: exploratory textual mention scoring only; no identity resolution

failure_semantics.rule: failures are counted and represented as empty predictions for recall; they are never silently discarded

runtime_fairness.technical_retries: At most one for MODEL_TIMEOUT or MODEL_SERVICE_FAILURE as defined in execution_config.json; never retry MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID.
runtime_fairness.latency: descriptive only unless hardware and runtime are comparable

statistics.rationale: fixed 100-narrative study; report exact numerators and denominators rather than adding underpowered inferential claims

forbidden_uses: create or tune a BERT adapter
leakage_policy.metric_bug: metric/tooling-only fixes are permitted if versioned and justified before interpreting results
leakage_policy.behavior_driven_change: contaminates this held-out set; relabel it DEV and create a new held-out set

reference_hardware_snapshot.cpu: Intel Core Ultra 7 258V, 8 cores, 8 logical processors
reference_hardware_snapshot.gpu: Intel Arc 140V GPU (driver-reported AdapterRAM 2147479552 bytes; shared-memory reporting caveat)
reference_hardware_snapshot.final_run_runtime: must be recorded at execution time

final_run_rule: No final system may run until an independent review authorizes the frozen protocol and dataset.
